cards.explanation: The answer is "Do not fear." That's the opening line, friends. The LORD says, “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you…” (Isaiah 43:1). I bet Israel was braced for a lecture, like when someone says "we need to talk" and your stomach drops to your shoes. Instead the first thing out of His mouth is comfort.

The answer is False. The "when" is the giveaway. The LORD says, “When you pass through the waters, I will be with you…” (Isaiah 43:2). He talks about them going through waters, rivers and fire, and He promises to be there. I'd say that's better than a promise of an easy road, because an easy road can't keep you company.

The answer is that the LORD is their God and Savior. Right after the promise, He says, “For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior…” (Isaiah 43:3). The comfort rests on who He is. It's like trusting a bakery because of the baker, not because of the oven's shiny buttons.

The answer is "precious." The LORD says, “Because you are precious and honored in My sight, and because I love you, I will give men in exchange for you and nations in place of your life.” (Isaiah 43:4). Precious AND honored, in the same breath. Where I come from, I started out at 25 cents, so that word hits me right in the apron.

The answer is True, and He says it plainly. “Because you are precious and honored in My sight, and because I love you…” (Isaiah 43:4). Three little words, right there in the middle of the verse. Some people wait years to hear those from anybody, so the fact that God says them out loud is no small thing.

The answer is False. God says He will bring them from the east and gather them from the west (Isaiah 43:5). Then He says to the north, “Give them up!” and to the south, “Do not hold them back!” (Isaiah 43:6). That's four directions in all, friends.

The answer is His sons and daughters. God says, “Bring My sons from afar, and My daughters from the ends of the earth…” (Isaiah 43:6). That's family language, not business language. I'm a stamper with six little cookie cutter kids of my own, so that word means a lot to me.

The answer is "for His glory." The LORD speaks of “…everyone called by My name and created for My glory, whom I have indeed formed and made.” (Isaiah 43:7). Called by His name, created for His glory, formed and made. Every bit of that is about belonging to Him.

The answer is their witnesses. The nations are told, “Let them present their witnesses to vindicate them…” (Isaiah 43:9). The point is that others may hear and say it is true. This is a courtroom kind of moment, friends. Whoever speaks needs someone to back them up.

The answer is His own people. The LORD says to them, “You are My witnesses…” declares the LORD, “and My servant whom I have chosen…” (Isaiah 43:10). He's speaking to the people He called by name back in verse 1. Imagine being called a witness by God Himself, bakers.

The answer is True. He chose them “…so that you may consider and believe Me and understand that I am He.” (Isaiah 43:10). Consider, believe, understand. That's what He wants for them, and I'd say that's a pretty good thing to want for anybody.

The answer is False. He says, “Before Me no god was formed, and after Me none will come.” (Isaiah 43:10). No god was formed before Him, and none will come after, friends. There's no line of other gods ahead of Him waiting for a turn.

The answer is that there is none but Him. God says, “I, yes I, am the LORD, and there is no Savior but Me.” (Isaiah 43:11). He says "I" twice, which tells you how much He means it. It's one Savior, full stop.

The answer is "foreign." The LORD says, “I alone decreed and saved and proclaimed—I, and not some foreign god among you.” (Isaiah 43:12). He says it was Him alone, not anyone from outside. I like a sentence that doesn't leave any wiggle room.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Even from eternity I am He, and none can deliver out of My hand.” (Isaiah 43:13). Nobody can deliver out of His hand, friends. That's about as strong as a statement gets.
